- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.prompt:
I need to find where memo metadata is computed/derived from memo content in this repository. This is metadata used for lists/previews that is computed rather than user-set. Search for:

1. Any "memo" related models, types, or interfaces that have derived/computed fields
2. Functions that compute or extract metadata from memo content (e.g., excerpts, previews, summaries)
3. Look for patterns like "excerpt", "preview", "summary", "snippet", "truncate" near memo-related code

Search breadth: very thorough. Look across the entire codebase for memo-related derived metadata computation.

I now have a comprehensive picture. Here is my report.

---

## Memo Derived/Computed Metadata -- Full Analysis

This repository (Memos -- an open-source note-taking service) computes several types of metadata from memo content. All computation happens server-side in Go, with one exception (heading extraction for outline navigation happens client-side in TypeScript). Below are all the locations, organized by type of derived metadata.

---

### 1. The `snippet` Field (Plain-Text Preview of Memo Content)

**Definition (protobuf):**
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` lines 265-266 -- `Memo.snippet` field marked `OUTPUT_ONLY`
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` lines 443-444 -- `MemoRelation.Memo.snippet` field marked `OUTPUT_ONLY`
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto` lines 815-835 -- `MemoCommentPayload.memo_snippet`, `MemoCommentPayload.related_memo_snippet`, `MemoMentionPayload.memo_snippet`, `MemoMentionPayload.related_memo_snippet`

**Core generation function:**
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` lines 263-346 -- `GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int)`. This parses markdown via goldmark, walks the AST to extract plain text (skipping code blocks, collapsing block elements with spaces), then calls `truncateAtWord` (line 472-489) if the result exceeds `maxLength`. Truncation is rune-aware for UTF-8 and breaks at word boundaries, appending ` ...`.

**Entry point into snippet generation:**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` lines 83-90 -- `getMemoContentSnippet(content string)` calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet(content, 64)` with a hardcoded max length of 64 characters.

**All call sites of `getMemoContentSnippet`:**
1. `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` line 76 -- when converting a single memo from store to API response (`convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators`)
2. `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` lines 225, 248 -- inside `batchConvertMemoRelations` for building snippets on related memos
3. `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go` lines 154, 162 -- `convertMemoRelationFromStore` fetches snippets for both sides of a relation
4. `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go` lines 318-328, 346-351, 374-391 -- `memoNotificationSnippet` used for comment and mention notification payloads

**Tests:**
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown_test.go` lines 52-183 -- `TestGenerateSnippet` with extensive cases (formatting stripping, code block removal, list items, inline code, images, autolinks, tags, truncation)
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown_test.go` lines 560-607 -- `TestTruncateAtWord` tests

---

### 2. The `Property` Field (Computed Boolean/String Properties)

**Definition (protobuf, stored in DB payload):**
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto` lines 7-23 -- `MemoPayload.Property` with:
  - `has_link` (bool)
  - `has_task_list` (bool)
  - `has_code` (bool)
  - `has_incomplete_tasks` (bool)
  - `title` (string) -- extracted from the first H1 heading

**API-facing definition:**
- `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` lines 272-279 -- `Memo.Property` message, marked `OUTPUT_ONLY`

**Core extraction function:**
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` lines 192-241 -- `ExtractProperties(content []byte)`. Walks the goldmark AST to detect:
  - `KindLink` nodes -> `HasLink = true`
  - `KindCodeBlock` / `KindFencedCodeBlock` / `KindCodeSpan` -> `HasCode = true`
  - `KindTaskCheckBox` (from GFM extension) -> `HasTaskList = true`; unchecked -> `HasIncompleteTasks = true`
  - First block-level child being an H1 heading -> `Title` extracted via `extractHeadingText` (line 173)

**Combined single-pass extraction:**
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` lines 355-422 -- `ExtractAll(content []byte)` returns `ExtractedData` containing `Tags`, `Mentions`, and `Property` all from a single AST walk. This is the preferred/efficient path.

**Where property computation is triggered:**
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` lines 74-88 -- `RebuildMemoPayload` calls `markdownService.ExtractAll()` and stores result in `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 108 -- called on **memo creation**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 447 -- called on **memo content update**
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` lines 27-72 -- `RunOnce()` batch-rebuilds payload for all memos (migration/recomputation)

**Conversion from store to API:**
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` lines 315-326 -- `convertMemoPropertyFromStore` maps store protobuf fields to API protobuf fields

**Tests:**
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown_test.go` lines 185-306 -- `TestExtractProperties`
- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown_test.go` lines 309-361 -- `TestExtractAllTitle`, `TestExtractAllMentions`, `TestExtractAllSkipsTagsInsideLinks`

---

### 3. Tags Extraction (Derived from Content)

Tags are extracted from memo content (not user-set) and stored in `MemoPayload.tags`.

- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` lines 142-170 -- `ExtractTags()` walks AST for `TagNode` instances
- Also extracted via `ExtractAll()` (line 377)
- Tag parsing is implemented via custom goldmark extensions at `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/extensions/tag.go` and `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/parser/tag.go`

---

### 4. Mentions Extraction (Derived from Content)

Mentions (`@username`) are extracted from memo content.

- `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` lines 379-380 in `ExtractAll()` -- detects `MentionNode` and lowercases usernames
- Mention parsing implemented at `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/extensions/mention.go` and `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/parser/mention.go`

---

### 5. RSS Feed Title Generation (Derived from Content)

- `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go` lines 302-336 -- `generateItemTitle(content string)` extracts the first line, strips markdown heading syntax (`# ` etc.), and truncates to 100 characters at a word boundary, appending `...`

---

### 6. Frontend: Heading Extraction for Outline Navigation

- `/bench/repo/web/src/utils/markdown-manipulation.ts` lines 108-154 -- `HeadingItem` interface and `extractHeadings(markdown)` function. Parses markdown via `micromark/mdast`, finds h1-h4 headings, computes slugs via `slugify()`, and deduplicates slug collisions with suffix numbering
- Used by `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoDetailSidebar/MemoOutline.tsx` for the sidebar heading outline

---

### 7. Frontend: Card Height Estimation (Derived from Content)

- `/bench/repo/web/src/components/PagedMemoList/memoCardHeight.ts` lines 40-110 -- `estimateMemoCardHeight()` and helpers. Computes estimated visual card height from content (line wrapping, markdown image counting), attachments, reactions, and comment relations for virtualized list rendering

---

### 8. Frontend: Share Image Preview Model (Derived from Memo)

- `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoActionMenu/memoShareImagePreviewModel.ts` -- `buildMemoShareImagePreviewModel()` derives a `MemoShareImagePreviewModel` from a memo's attachments (visual vs. non-visual grouping, footer badge counts, display time formatting)

---

### 9. Frontend: Snippet Resolution for Relations

- `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoMetadata/Relation/useResolvedRelationMemos.ts` -- `useResolvedRelationMemos()` hook detects relations that lack a `snippet` field and fetches the full memo to hydrate the snippet for display
- Snippets are consumed by `MemoSnippetLink` (`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoView/components/MemoSnippetLink.tsx`) and the `MemoDetailSidebar` (`/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoDetailSidebar/MemoDetailSidebar.tsx` line 155)

---

### Summary of Key Files

| Purpose | File |
|---|---|
| **Snippet generation** (core) | `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` (lines 263-346, 470-489) |
| **Property extraction** (core) | `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` (lines 192-241) |
| **Combined extraction** (tags + props + mentions) | `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` (lines 355-422) |
| **Payload rebuild trigger** | `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` |
| **Snippet call site wrapper** | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` (lines 83-90) |
| **Store-to-API conversion** (snippet + property) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` |
| **Notification snippets** | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go` (lines 318-396) |
| **Relation snippets** | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go` (lines 149-177) |
| **RSS title derivation** | `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go` (lines 302-336) |
| **Protobuf: snippet field** | `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` (lines 265-266, 443-444) |
| **Protobuf: property field** | `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto` (lines 15-23) |
| **Protobuf: notification snippets** | `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto` (lines 815-835) |
| **Store model** | `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` (lines 35-55) |
| **Frontend: heading extraction** | `/bench/repo/web/src/utils/markdown-manipulation.ts` (lines 108-154) |
| **Frontend: card height estimation** | `/bench/repo/web/src/components/PagedMemoList/memoCardHeight.ts` |
| **Frontend: share preview model** | `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoActionMenu/memoShareImagePreviewModel.ts` |
| **Frontend: snippet hydration** | `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoMetadata/Relation/useResolvedRelationMemos.ts` |
| **Tests** | `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown_test.go` |

The derived metadata is computed in two places, both in `internal/markdown/markdown.go`:

1. **`MemoPayload.Property`** — extracted by `ExtractProperties()` (lines 192–241), or more commonly via the combined single-pass `ExtractAll()` (lines 355–422), which walks the goldmark AST and populates:

   - `has_task_list` (bool) — whether the content contains task checkboxes
   - `has_code` (bool) — whether the content contains code blocks or code spans
   - `has_incomplete_tasks` (bool) — whether any task checkboxes are unchecked

2. **`snippet`** — generated by `GenerateSnippet()` (lines 263–346), which parses the markdown AST, extracts plain text (skipping code blocks, collapsing block elements), and truncates to 64 characters at a word boundary (appending ` ...`). The entry point is `getMemoContentSnippet()` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:83–90`.

**Computation site:** `internal/markdown/markdown.go` — functions `ExtractAll()`/`ExtractProperties()` for the property, and `GenerateSnippet()` for the snippet. The payload rebuild is orchestrated by `RebuildMemoPayload()` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74–88`.

**Triggers:** Recomputation is triggered on **memo creation** (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`) and **memo content update** (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`). A batch rebuild path (`RunOnce()` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27–72`) recomputes for all memos (used for migration/reindexing). The snippet is additionally computed at conversion time in `memo_service_converter.go:76` and for relation/notification payloads.

**Extracted properties:** `has_link`, `has_task_list`, `has_code`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, `title` (first H1 heading text), and `snippet` (plain-text preview truncated to 64 chars).
